passage.title: A MORNING AT THE CORNER BAKERY
passage.subtitle: Sofia's weekend job in Bristol
paragraphs: Every Saturday and Sunday, eighteen-year-old Sofia wakes up at half past five to help at her aunt Clara's bakery in Bristol. The bakery is on a quiet street near the river, and local people love going there for warm bread and sweet pastries.

Sofia arrives at six o'clock, puts on her white apron, and helps arrange the croissants on wooden trays. Her aunt bakes three kinds of bread every morning: white bread, brown bread, and cheese bread. By seven o'clock, the sweet smell of coffee and butter fills the whole shop.

The busiest time is between eight and ten in the morning, when office workers and families stop by for breakfast. Sofia takes orders at the counter and packs cakes into small boxes. She says her favourite customers are the schoolchildren who come in with their parents for hot chocolate.

At two o'clock in the afternoon, the bakery closes. Before going home, Sofia cleans the tables and counts the remaining rolls. Clara always gives her a small bag of fresh biscuits as a thank-you gift.
